% ================================================================
% Retrieval starters for a Year 10 mixed higher/foundation class,
% used across the algebraic fractions unit.
%
% Every starter draws on each of the three earlier topics: prime factor
% decomposition (factor trees, and HCF and LCM from Venn diagrams),
% indices (the index laws, negative and fractional indices) and surds
% (simplifying, adding, subtracting and multiplying). Each number skill
% is set beside the algebra it becomes once the fractions have letters
% in them. The five starters follow the order of the unit:
%
%   1  HCF and cancelling           -> simplifying single-term fractions
%   2  index laws                   -> dividing powers, negative indices
%   3  surds and single brackets    -> simplifying by factorising
%   4  double brackets              -> simplifying by factorising a quadratic
%   5  LCM and fraction arithmetic  -> adding, subtracting, multiplying
%                                      and dividing
%
% Within each starter the questions run from foundation to higher. A
% question marked (Extension) is higher tier, and the last question on
% each starter is a challenge that connects to the lesson.
% ================================================================

\setbeamertemplate{navigation symbols}{}
\setbeamersize{text margin left=0.4cm, text margin right=0.4cm}
\setlength{\multicolsep}{4pt}
\setlength{\columnsep}{20pt}

% ================================================================
% Answer-overlay helpers
% ================================================================
\newcommand{\ablank}[1]{%
  \alt<2>{\textcolor{red}{#1}}{\underline{\phantom{#1}}}%
}
\newcommand{\ashow}[1]{\uncover<2->{\textcolor{red}{\small #1}}}
\newcommand{\ashowq}[1]{\alt<2->{\textcolor{red}{\small #1}}{?}}

% Answers drawn straight on to a TikZ diagram, revealed on overlay 2 like \ashow.
% Space is reserved on overlay 1, so the diagram does not move between slides.
\usetikzlibrary{overlay-beamer-styles}
\tikzset{
  ans/.style     = {red, thick, visible on=<2->},
  ansfill/.style = {red!15, visible on=<2->},
  anslab/.style  = {red, font=\tiny, visible on=<2->},
}

% Used by the worked solutions rather than by this deck, so that each worked
% solution is first a question with room to write in and then the answer.
\newlength{\aworkpad}
\setlength{\aworkpad}{8mm}
\newcommand{\awork}[1]{%
  \par\vspace{\aworkpad}%
  \uncover<2->{#1}%
  \par\vspace{\aworkpad}%
}

% A gap drawn as a dotted box, for blanks inside a fraction or a chain of
% working. An \ablank underline sits on top of a fraction bar and reads as a
% second bar, so these gaps are boxed instead. The answer appears in red
% inside the box on overlay 2.
\newcommand{\abox}[1]{%
  \tikz[baseline=(b.base)]\node[draw=gray, densely dotted, inner sep=1.5pt] (b)
    {\alt<2->{\textcolor{red}{#1}}{\phantom{#1}}};%
}

% Every question list on these slides is tight, so that the diagram column and
% the question column both finish inside the slide.
\newcommand{\tightlist}{%
  \setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}\setlength{\topsep}{0pt}%
}

% Factor trees. A composite number is written plainly and a prime is circled.
% The gaps are dotted: a box for a composite number and a circle for a prime.
\tikzset{
  tnum/.style   = {inner sep=1.5pt, font=\scriptsize},
  tprime/.style = {circle, draw, inner sep=0.5pt, minimum size=0.42cm, font=\scriptsize},
  tgap/.style   = {draw=gray, densely dotted, minimum width=0.5cm,
                   minimum height=0.36cm, inner sep=0pt},
  tpgap/.style  = {circle, draw=gray, densely dotted, minimum size=0.42cm, inner sep=0pt},
}

% Venn diagrams of prime factors, and the headings above each diagram.
% The set labels are anchored on the outside of each circle so that they
% stay clear of its edge however long the label is.
\tikzset{
  vleft/.style  = {thick, blue!60!black},
  vright/.style = {thick, orange!80!black},
  vlabl/.style  = {blue!60!black, anchor=east},
  vlabr/.style  = {orange!80!black, anchor=west},
  dhead/.style  = {font=\scriptsize\bfseries, anchor=west},
  vans/.style   = {anslab, font=\scriptsize},
}

\usepackage{xcolor}

\definecolor{ealkeycolour}{RGB}{0,128,0}

\newsavebox{\ealboxen}

\newlength{\ealglosswd}
\newlength{\ealglossraise}

% a tier 3 word, in English and in translation alike
\newcommand{\ealkey}[1]{\textcolor{ealkeycolour}{#1}}
\newcommand{\ealkeytr}[1]{\textcolor{ealkeycolour}{\ealtext{#1}}}

% One translated word above one English word. Built from kernel
% primitives, never a tabular, which would break wherever the sheet
% loads array, booktabs or tabularx. The box is as wide as the wider of
% the two, so a long translation pushes its neighbours aside instead of
% overlapping them, and it claims its full height so a table row or a
% TikZ node makes room for it.
\newcommand{\ealgloss}[2]{%
  \sbox{\ealboxen}{\ealkey{#1}}%
  \sbox{\ealboxtr}{\small\textcolor{ealtwocolour}{\ealtext{#2}}}%
  \setlength{\ealglosswd}{\wd\ealboxen}%
  \ifdim\wd\ealboxtr>\ealglosswd\setlength{\ealglosswd}{\wd\ealboxtr}\fi
  \leavevmode
  \makebox[\ealglosswd][c]{%
    \makebox[0pt][c]{\usebox{\ealboxen}}%
    \makebox[0pt][c]{\raisebox{\ealglossraise}{\usebox{\ealboxtr}}}%
  }%
}

% opens up line spacing around a block of glosses, so the raised
% translations sit clear of the line above
\newenvironment{ealglossed}{\par\linespread{2.1}\selectfont\ignorespaces}{\par}

% a whole translated sentence above its English counterpart. block level,
% so it does not belong inside a tabular cell
\newcommand{\ealpara}[2]{%
  \par\addvspace{0.5\baselineskip}%
  {\color{ealtwocolour}\ealtextblock{#1}}%
  \penalty200
  {\color{ealenglish}#2\par}%
  \addvspace{0.5\baselineskip}%
}

\begin{frame}[t]{Starter 1: \ealgloss{Prime Factors}{czynniki pierwsze} \& \ealgloss{HCF}{największy wspólny dzielnik} (1 of 3)}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]

\column{0.36\textwidth}
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{center}
\vspace{-0.6em}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9, every node/.style={font=\scriptsize}]
\node[dhead] at (-1.2,0.45) {\ealgloss{Factor tree}{drzewko czynników}};
\node[tnum]   (t84) at (0,0)       {$84$};
\node[tprime] (t2a) at (-0.6,-0.6) {$2$};
\node[tnum]   (t42) at (0.6,-0.6)  {$42$};
\node[tprime] (t2b) at (0,-1.2)    {$2$};
\node[tgap]   (t21) at (1.2,-1.2)  {};

\draw (t84) -- (t2a);  \draw (t84) -- (t42);

\column{0.64\textwidth}
\vspace{-1.5em}
\footnotesize
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}\tightlist
  \item \ealgloss{Simplify}{uprościć} $\sqrt{20}$.
        \ashow{$\sqrt{4\times5}=2\sqrt{5}$}
  \item Work out $2^{-1}$ and $9^{\frac12}$.
        \ashow{$\dfrac12$ and $3$}
  \item Complete the \ealgloss{factor tree}{drzewko czynników}. Write $84$ as a \ealgloss{product}{iloczyn} of \ealgloss{prime factors}{czynniki pierwsze} in \ealgloss{index}{wykładnik} form.
        \ashow{$84=2^2\times3\times7$}
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Starter 1: \ealgloss{Prime Factors}{czynniki pierwsze} \& \ealgloss{HCF}{największy wspólny dzielnik} (2 of 3)}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]

\column{0.36\textwidth}
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{center}
\vspace{-0.6em}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9, every node/.style={font=\scriptsize}]
\node[dhead] at (-1.2,1.2) {\ealgloss{Venn diagram}{diagram Venna} A};
\draw[vleft]  (0,0)   circle (0.8);
\draw[vright] (1.0,0) circle (0.8);
\node[vlabl] at (-0.45,0.85) {$60$};
\node[vlabr] at (1.45,0.85)  {$84$};
\node at (-0.35,0)   {$5$};
\node at (0.5,0.35)  {$2$};
\node[vans] at (0.5,0)     {$2$};
\node[vans] at (0.5,-0.35) {$3$};
\node[vans] at (1.35,0)    {$7$};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\end{ealglossed}

\column{0.64\textwidth}
\vspace{-1.5em}
\footnotesize
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}\tightlist
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
  \item $60=2^2\times3\times5$. Complete \ealgloss{Venn diagram}{diagram Venna} A for $60$ and $84$, then find the \ealgloss{HCF}{największy wspólny dzielnik} and the \ealgloss{LCM}{najmniejsza wspólna wielokrotność} of $60$ and $84$.
        \ashow{\ealgloss{HCF}{największy wspólny dzielnik} $=12$; \; \ealgloss{LCM}{najmniejsza wspólna wielokrotność} $=2^2\times3\times5\times7=420$}
  \item \ealgloss{Simplify}{uprościć} $\dfrac{60}{84}$ by dividing by the \ealgloss{HCF}{największy wspólny dzielnik}. Which numbers in \ealgloss{Venn diagram}{diagram Venna} A are not in the \ealgloss{HCF}{największy wspólny dzielnik}?
        \ashow{$\dfrac{5}{7}$: the $5$ and the $7$, which are not shared}
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Starter 1: \ealgloss{Prime Factors}{czynniki pierwsze} \& \ealgloss{HCF}{największy wspólny dzielnik} (3 of 3)}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]

\column{0.36\textwidth}
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{center}
\vspace{-0.6em}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9, every node/.style={font=\scriptsize}]
\node[dhead] at (-1.2,1.2) {\ealgloss{Venn diagram}{diagram Venna} B};
\draw[vleft]  (0,0)   circle (0.8);
\draw[vright] (1.0,0) circle (0.8);
\node[vlabl] at (-0.45,0.85) {$6a^2b$};
\node[vlabr] at (1.45,0.85)  {$9ab^2$};
\node[vans] at (-0.35,0.18)  {$2$};
\node[vans] at (-0.35,-0.18) {$a$};
\node[vans] at (0.5,0.35)    {$3$};
\node[vans] at (0.5,0)       {$a$};
\node[vans] at (0.5,-0.35)   {$b$};
\node[vans] at (1.35,0.18)   {$3$};
\node[vans] at (1.35,-0.18)  {$b$};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\end{ealglossed}

\column{0.64\textwidth}
\vspace{-1.5em}
\footnotesize
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}\tightlist
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
  \item \ealgloss{Simplify}{uprościć} $\dfrac{x^5}{x^2}$ by writing out the $x$s and \ealgloss{cancelling}{skracanie}.
        \ashow{$x^2$ cancels from the top and the bottom, leaving $x^3=x^{5-2}$}
  \item (Challenge) Complete \ealgloss{Venn diagram}{diagram Venna} B for $6a^2b$ and $9ab^2$. Use it to \ealgloss{simplify}{uprościć} $\dfrac{6a^2b}{9ab^2}$.
        \ashow{The \ealgloss{HCF}{największy wspólny dzielnik} is $3ab$, so $\dfrac{6a^2b}{9ab^2}=\dfrac{2a}{3b}$}
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

%------------------------------------------------------------------
% STARTER 2: Index laws on cubes, cuboids and squares
%------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{frame}[t]{Starter 2: \ealgloss{Index}{wykładnik} Laws (1 of 3)}
\vspace{-1.5em}
\footnotesize
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}\tightlist
  \item Write $72$ as a \ealgloss{product}{iloczyn} of \ealgloss{prime factors}{czynniki pierwsze} in \ealgloss{index}{wykładnik} form.
        \ashow{$72=2^3\times3^2$}
  \item \ealgloss{Simplify}{uprościć} $\sqrt{8}+\sqrt{18}$.
        \ashow{$2\sqrt{2}+3\sqrt{2}=5\sqrt{2}$}
  \item \ealgloss{Simplify}{uprościć} $x^4\times x^3$ and $y^8\div y^2$.
        \ashow{$x^7$ and $y^6$}
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Starter 2: \ealgloss{Index}{wykładnik} Laws (2 of 3)}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]

\column{0.36\textwidth}
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{center}
\vspace{-0.6em}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8, every node/.style={font=\scriptsize}]
\node[dhead] at (-0.1,1.8) {\ealgloss{Cube}{sześcian}};
\draw[fill=blue!8]  (0,0) rectangle (1.1,1.1);
\draw[fill=blue!16] (0,1.1) -- (0.4,1.4) -- (1.5,1.4) -- (1.1,1.1) -- cycle;
\draw[fill=blue!4]  (1.1,0) -- (1.5,0.3) -- (1.5,1.4) -- (1.1,1.1) -- cycle;
\node[below] at (0.55,0) {$2x$};

\begin{scope}[xshift=2.45cm]
\node[dhead] at (-0.1,1.8) {\ealgloss{Cuboid}{prostopadłościan}};
\draw[fill=orange!10] (0,0) rectangle (1.5,0.8);
\draw[fill=orange!20] (0,0.8) -- (0.5,1.15) -- (2.0,1.15) -- (1.5,0.8) -- cycle;
\draw[fill=orange!5]  (1.5,0) -- (2.0,0.35) -- (2.0,1.15) -- (1.5,0.8) -- cycle;
\node[below] at (0.75,0) {$3x$};
\node[left, inner sep=1pt] at (0,0.4) {$x^2$};
\node[below right, inner sep=1pt] at (1.75,0.17) {$2x$};
\end{scope}
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\end{ealglossed}

\column{0.64\textwidth}
\vspace{-1.5em}
\footnotesize
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}\tightlist
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
  \item Write $2^{-3}$ and $x^{-2}$ as \ealgloss{fractions}{ułamki}.
        \ashow{$\dfrac18$ and $\dfrac{1}{x^2}$}
  \item Find the \ealgloss{volume}{objętość} of the \ealgloss{cube}{sześcian}. Is it $2x^3$ or $8x^3$?
        \ashow{$(2x)^3=2^3x^3=8x^3$}
  \item Find the \ealgloss{volume}{objętość} of the \ealgloss{cuboid}{prostopadłościan}.
        \ashow{$3x\times2x\times x^2=6x^4$}
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Starter 2: \ealgloss{Index}{wykładnik} Laws (3 of 3)}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]

\column{0.36\textwidth}
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{center}
\vspace{-0.6em}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8, every node/.style={font=\scriptsize}]
\node[dhead] at (-0.1,1.9) {\ealgloss{Square}{podnieść do kwadratu; kwadrat}};
\draw[fill=green!8] (0,0) rectangle (1.6,1.6);
\node at (0.8,1.0)  {\ealgloss{Area}{pole}};
\node at (0.8,0.6)  {$36x^4$};
\node[left] at (0,0.8) {$?$};
\node[vans, below] at (0.8,0) {$6x^2$};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\end{ealglossed}

\column{0.64\textwidth}
\vspace{-1.5em}
\footnotesize
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}\tightlist
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
  \item The \ealgloss{square}{podnieść do kwadratu; kwadrat} has \ealgloss{area}{pole} $36x^4$, so its side length is $\left(36x^4\right)^{\frac12}$. \ealgloss{Simplify}{uprościć} this.
        \ashow{$36^{\frac12}\times x^{4\times\frac12}=6x^2$}
  \item (Extension) Complete the working.\\[2pt]
        \hspace*{1em}$8^{-\frac23}=\dfrac{1}{8^{\frac23}}=\dfrac{1}{\left(\sqrt[3]{8}\right)^2}
        =\dfrac{1}{\abox{$2$}^{\,2}}=\abox{$\dfrac14$}$
  \item (Challenge) Divide the \ealgloss{volume}{objętość} of the \ealgloss{cube}{sześcian} by the \ealgloss{volume}{objętość} of the \ealgloss{cuboid}{prostopadłościan}. Write the answer as a \ealgloss{fraction}{ułamek} in its \ealgloss{simplest form}{najprostsza postać}.
        \ashow{$\dfrac{8x^3}{6x^4}=\dfrac{4}{3x}$}
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\draw[fill=blue!6] (0,0) rectangle (0.55,0.55);
\draw[fill=blue!6] (0.55,0) rectangle (1.75,0.55);
\node[above] at (0.275,0.55) {$\sqrt{2}$};
\node[above] at (1.15,0.55)  {$3$};
\node[left]  at (0,0.275)    {$\sqrt{2}$};
\node[vans] at (0.275,0.275) {$2$};
\node[vans] at (1.15,0.275)  {$3\sqrt{2}$};
\end{scope}
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\end{ealglossed}

\column{0.62\textwidth}
\vspace{-1.5em}
\footnotesize
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}\tightlist
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
  \item Use the \ealgloss{prime factors}{czynniki pierwsze} to \ealgloss{simplify}{uprościć} $\sqrt{180}$.\\[1pt]
        \ashow{$\sqrt{2^2\times3^2\times5}=2\times3\times\sqrt{5}=6\sqrt{5}$}
  \item The \ealgloss{square}{podnieść do kwadratu; kwadrat} has \ealgloss{area}{pole} $50$\,cm$^2$. Find its side length as a \ealgloss{simplified}{uproszczony} \ealgloss{surd}{pierwiastek niewymierny}, and its \ealgloss{perimeter}{obwód}.\\[1pt]
        \ashow{$\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt{2}$\,cm; \; $4\times5\sqrt{2}=20\sqrt{2}$\,cm}
  \item Complete rectangle A to \ealgloss{expand}{wymnażać nawiasy} $\sqrt{2}(\sqrt{2}+3)$.
        \ashow{$2+3\sqrt{2}$}
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Starter 3: \ealgloss{Surds}{pierwiastki niewymierne} \& Single \ealgloss{Brackets}{nawiasy} (3 of 3)}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]

\column{0.38\textwidth}
\begin{ealglossed}

\vspace{-0.6em}

\node at (1.6,0.275) {$15$};
\node[vans] at (bl) {$2x$};
\node[vans] at (br) {$5$};
\end{scope}

\end{center}
\end{ealglossed}

\column{0.62\textwidth}
\vspace{-1.5em}
\footnotesize
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}\tightlist
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
  \item Complete rectangle B to \ealgloss{factorise}{rozkładać na czynniki} $6x+15$. Then \ealgloss{simplify}{uprościć} $\dfrac{6x+15}{3}$.
        \ashow{$3(2x+5)$; \; $2x+5$, not $2x+15$}
  \item (Challenge) Sam says $\dfrac{6+\sqrt{18}}{3}=2+\sqrt{18}$. Explain Sam's mistake, then \ealgloss{simplify}{uprościć} it correctly.
        \ashow{Divide both \ealgloss{terms}{wyrazy} by $3$: \; $2+\dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{3}=2+\sqrt{2}$}
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\node[vans] at (1.45,-1.25) {$10$};

\end{ealglossed}

\column{0.64\textwidth}
\vspace{-1.5em}
\footnotesize
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}\tightlist
  \item Is $3^{-2}$ equal to $-9$, $-6$ or $\frac19$?
        \ashow{$\dfrac{1}{3^2}=\dfrac19$}
  \item \ealgloss{Simplify}{uprościć} $\sqrt{50}-\sqrt{8}$. Is it $\sqrt{42}$?
        \ashow{No: $5\sqrt{2}-2\sqrt{2}=3\sqrt{2}$}
  \item Complete grid A to \ealgloss{expand}{wymnażać nawiasy} $(x+2)(x+5)$.
        \ashow{$x^2+7x+10$}
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}

\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Starter 4: Double \ealgloss{Brackets}{nawiasy} (2 of 3)}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]

\column{0.36\textwidth}
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{center}
\vspace{-0.6em}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9, every node/.style={font=\scriptsize}]
\begin{scope}[yshift=-2.6cm]
\node[dhead] at (-0.5,0.75) {Grid B};
\draw[fill=orange!8] (0,0)      rectangle (1.0,-1.0);
\draw[fill=orange!8] (1.0,0)    rectangle (1.9,-1.0);
\draw[fill=orange!8] (0,-1.0)   rectangle (1.0,-1.5);
\draw[fill=orange!8] (1.0,-1.0) rectangle (1.9,-1.5);
\node[above] at (0.5,0) {$x$};
\node[tgap] (gt) at (1.45,0.3) {};
\node[left]  at (0,-0.5) {$x$};
\node[tgap] (gl) at (-0.42,-1.25) {};
\node at (0.5,-0.5)   {$x^2$};
\node at (1.45,-1.25) {$12$};
\node[font=\scriptsize] at (0.95,-1.85) {\ealgloss{Area}{pole} $=x^2+7x+12$};
\node[vans] at (gt) {$4$};
\node[vans] at (gl) {$3$};
\node[vans] at (1.45,-0.5) {$4x$};
\node[vans] at (0.5,-1.25) {$3x$};
\end{scope}
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\end{ealglossed}

\column{0.64\textwidth}
\vspace{-1.5em}
\footnotesize
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}\tightlist
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
  \item Write $12$ as a \ealgloss{product}{iloczyn} of \ealgloss{prime factors}{czynniki pierwsze}, then list its \ealgloss{factor pairs}{pary czynników}. Which pair adds to $7$?
        \ashow{$2^2\times3$; \; $1\times12$, $2\times6$, $3\times4$; \; $3+4=7$}
  \item Complete grid B to \ealgloss{factorise}{rozkładać na czynniki} $x^2+7x+12$.
        \ashow{$(x+3)(x+4)$, in either order}
  \item A rectangle has \ealgloss{area}{pole} $x^2+7x+12$ and width $x+3$. Find its length.
        Use this to \ealgloss{simplify}{uprościć} $\dfrac{x^2+7x+12}{x+3}$.\\[2pt]
        \ashow{$\dfrac{(x+3)(x+4)}{x+3}=x+4$}
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Starter 4: Double \ealgloss{Brackets}{nawiasy} (3 of 3)}
\vspace{-1.5em}
\footnotesize
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}\tightlist
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
  \item \ealgloss{Factorise}{rozkładać na czynniki} $x^2-9$. Use the \ealgloss{difference of two squares}{różnica dwóch kwadratów} to \ealgloss{expand}{wymnażać nawiasy} $(3+\sqrt{2})(3-\sqrt{2})$.
        \ashow{$(x+3)(x-3)$; \; $9-2=7$}
  \item (Challenge) $391=20^2-3^2$. Use this to write $391$ as a \ealgloss{product}{iloczyn} of \ealgloss{prime factors}{czynniki pierwsze}.
        \ashow{$(20+3)(20-3)=23\times17$, both \ealgloss{prime}{liczba pierwsza}}
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{frame}

%------------------------------------------------------------------
% STARTER 5: The LCM as a common denominator, and the four operations
%------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{frame}[t]{Starter 5: \ealgloss{LCM}{najmniejsza wspólna wielokrotność} \& \ealgloss{Fractions}{ułamki} (1 of 3)}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]

\column{0.36\textwidth}
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{center}
\vspace{-0.6em}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9, every node/.style={font=\scriptsize}]
\node[dhead] at (-1.2,1.2) {\ealgloss{Venn diagram}{diagram Venna} A};
\draw[vleft]  (0,0)   circle (0.8);
\draw[vright] (1.0,0) circle (0.8);
\node[vlabl] at (-0.45,0.85) {$12$};
\node[vlabr] at (1.45,0.85)  {$18$};
\node at (-0.35,0)  {$2$};
\node at (0.5,0.18) {$2$};
\node[vans] at (0.5,-0.18) {$3$};
\node[vans] at (1.35,0)    {$3$};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\end{ealglossed}

\column{0.64\textwidth}
\vspace{-1.5em}
\footnotesize
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}\tightlist
  \item \ealgloss{Simplify}{uprościć} $a^3\times a^{-1}$.
        \ashow{$a^{3+(-1)}=a^2$}
  \item Work out $\sqrt{8}\times\sqrt{2}$.
        \ashow{$\sqrt{16}=4$}
  \item $12=2^2\times3$ and $18=2\times3^2$. Complete \ealgloss{Venn diagram}{diagram Venna} A, then find the \ealgloss{HCF}{największy wspólny dzielnik} and the \ealgloss{LCM}{najmniejsza wspólna wielokrotność} of $12$ and $18$.
        \ashow{\ealgloss{HCF}{największy wspólny dzielnik} $=6$; \; \ealgloss{LCM}{najmniejsza wspólna wielokrotność} $=2^2\times3^2=36$}
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Starter 5: \ealgloss{LCM}{najmniejsza wspólna wielokrotność} \& \ealgloss{Fractions}{ułamki} (2 of 3)}
\vspace{-1.5em}
\footnotesize
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}\tightlist
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
  \item Complete: \;
        $\dfrac{5}{12}+\dfrac{7}{18}=\dfrac{\abox{$15$}}{36}+\dfrac{\abox{$14$}}{36}
        =\dfrac{\abox{$29$}}{36}$
  \item Write $\dfrac{x}{12}-\dfrac{x}{18}$ as a single \ealgloss{fraction}{ułamek}.\\
        \ashow{$\dfrac{3x}{36}-\dfrac{2x}{36}=\dfrac{x}{36}$}
  \item Work out $\dfrac34\times\dfrac89$. Then \ealgloss{simplify}{uprościć} $\dfrac{3x}{4}\div\dfrac{9x}{10}$.\\
        \ashow{$\dfrac{24}{36}=\dfrac23$; \;
               $\dfrac{3x}{4}\times\dfrac{10}{9x}=\dfrac{30x}{36x}=\dfrac56$}
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Starter 5: \ealgloss{LCM}{najmniejsza wspólna wielokrotność} \& \ealgloss{Fractions}{ułamki} (3 of 3)}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]

\column{0.36\textwidth}
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{center}
\vspace{-0.6em}

\draw[vleft]  (0,0)   circle (0.8);
\draw[vright] (1.0,0) circle (0.8);
\node[vlabl] at (-0.45,0.85) {$4x$};
\node[vlabr] at (1.45,0.85)  {$6x^2$};
\node[vans] at (-0.35,0)     {$2$};
\node[vans] at (0.5,0.18)    {$2$};
\node[vans] at (0.5,-0.18)   {$x$};
\node[vans] at (1.35,0.18)   {$3$};
\node[vans] at (1.35,-0.18)  {$x$};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\end{ealglossed}

\column{0.64\textwidth}
\vspace{-1.5em}
\footnotesize
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}\tightlist
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
  \item $4x=2\times2\times x$ and $6x^2=2\times3\times x\times x$. Complete \ealgloss{Venn diagram}{diagram Venna} B, then find the \ealgloss{LCM}{najmniejsza wspólna wielokrotność} of $4x$ and $6x^2$.
        \ashow{$2\times2\times3\times x\times x=12x^2$}
  \item (Challenge) Write $\dfrac{5}{4x}+\dfrac{1}{6x^2}$ as a single \ealgloss{fraction}{ułamek}.
        \ashow{$\dfrac{15x}{12x^2}+\dfrac{2}{12x^2}=\dfrac{15x+2}{12x^2}$}
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}
